claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 begins cooling in a high-temperature single-phase BCC state.
Short-range-order kinetics during cooling control phase transformations in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Slow cooling promotes more SRO-cluster development than rapid quenching.
The proposed SRO clusters contain transition-metal atoms and aluminum.
SRO clusters lower local free-energy barriers for secondary-phase formation.
SRO clusters act as nucleation sites or precursors for secondary precipitates.
Rapid quenching suppresses or minimizes SRO by freezing the high-temperature atomic configuration.
Rapid quenching preserves a primarily metastable BCC structure in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Moderate subsequent thermal exposure can permit ordering and precipitation processes to evolve.
The proposed mechanism may not apply during reheating to high temperatures.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when alloy composition or atomic interactions do not favor significant SRO.
Slow-cooled samples will exhibit more secondary-phase formation than rapidly quenched samples.
Secondary-phase formation can be observed through additional diffraction peaks or distinct phase-separated microstructural features.
The rapidly quenched baseline will have a uniform BCC microstructure, minimal detectable SRO, and no or minimal secondary phases.
The controlled comparison consists of rapid quenching and slow cooling from the same high-temperature state, followed by identical intermediate-temperature exposures.
XRD, TEM, and APT can respectively assess phase constitution, microstructure or precipitates, and SRO or compositional variation.
A lack of statistically significant phase or microstructural differences between slow-cooled and quenched samples would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The boundary permits a null result whenever the thermal history provides insufficient time for ordering, but the experiment does not quantify cooling rates, exposure temperature, or duration and nevertheless declares any null phase or microstructural result falsifying. Thus the stated escape condition can make the proposed falsification non-decisive.
